result.title: Bots in the boardroom: How AI is changing how boards make decisions
result.description:
Should your board appoint a bot? In some cases, bots are already there, being put to work helping directors dig through board packs, challenge bias and spot hidden risks. While mostly used for research and observation (and are not voting members), these tools still raise difficult questions about confidentiality, legal privilege, and accountability, and what governance will require in the years ahead. How can boards use AI to widen their perspectives without replacing human judgment or surrendering fiduciary responsibility?

Miriam Vogel, president and CEO of EqualAI, and Helle Bank Jørgensen, global managing director at Board Intelligence, discuss this complex issue, covering:

- How ‘bots’ are being leveraged by modern boards already to navigate increasingly lengthy board packs, challenge groupthink, uncover inconsistencies and ask better questions
- What to consider when introducing AI into decision making - including confidentiality, legal privilege, AI hallucinations and accuracy
- How board makeup might evolve with AI’s expanded use and how the responsibilities for chairpeople will change
The practical guardrails boards need, including visibility into AI use, audit trails and more
- How expanded AI literacy can help boards maximize new technologies while tackling governance responsibilities

result.description:
This week's top stories of the week include:

00:14 - This colourful school is also a power plant:
Today, any building can become a renewable power plant. This design approach is called building-integrated photovoltaics - and it could turn the world’s built environment into a vast clean energy resource. Here are 3 striking examples.

01:55 - The top finance stories you need to know:
Global finance is being tested. Digital editor Spencer Feingold breaks down the latest developments being tracked by the World Economic Forum's Centre for Financial and Monetary Systems.

03:27 - Fewer than a third of the world’s CEOs are women, UN data shows:
Women hold just 31% of #management positions worldwide, according to a new survey by the ILO. This is despite the fact that businesses led by a female #CEO are 6% more likely to report higher profits - while those with a female chair are 18% more likely.

04:53 - This new glue could make batteries greener:
Recycling lithium batteries could one day be as simple as soaking them in water. Researchers at UC San Diego have developed a new water-soluble glue that could make #lithium batteries easier to recycle - without compromising performance.

result.title: We all depend on the construction industry. Here’s why it urgently needs more workers
result.description:
Ebru Özdemir, chair of infrastructure company Limak, explains why ‘maker skills’ are becoming ever more vital to the 21st-century economy.

‘Maker skills’ are the practical abilities that power the physical economy, from constructing and installing to operating equipment and processing materials. Demand for them is rising faster than supply. The World Economic Forum’s The First Mile Sandbox aims to foster talent pipelines by connecting universities with employers and other stakeholders.
